summary: This task's own branch diff is limited to PROGRESS.md, rewriting the tracking file to document that PR23 and PR24 (owned by two other, separate worker branches) had real merge conflicts against origin/master which were resolved and pushed directly to those branches, with PR23 left for the normal automated pipeline and PR24 explicitly deferred to the Owner for the merge decision per task constraints -- consistent with the tiered-trust model's requirement that workers never merge to main themselves. The PROGRESS.md content itself is internally consistent, correctly scoped (no attempt to merge PR24 to master), and does not touch .github/workflows/** so the hard workflow-scope rule is not implicated. The material limitation is that the actual conflict-resolution diffs (PROGRESS.md stub, AUDITOR_ENGINE_PHASE_PLAN add/add conflict, MASTER_INDEX.yaml registries entry, CRONTAB_APPROVED_SNAPSHOT.txt/OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED auto-merges) live on the PR23 and PR24 branches themselves, not in this diff, so this review cannot verify their correctness first-hand and is relying on the worker's self-report for that substance -- those two PRs need their own independent diff review (ideally re-confirming gh pr view mergeable/mergeStateStatus directly) before a human signs off on merging either.
issues: The reviewed diff contains no actual conflict-resolution content -- it is a self-report in PROGRESS.md describing work already pushed to two other branches (PR23, PR24). Per the dispatch prompt's own rule to review the actual diff and not trust a self-report, those two PRs' real diffs (especially PR24's AUDITOR_ENGINE_PHASE_PLAN and MASTER_INDEX.yaml conflict resolutions, and the security-scanner/cron content) should be independently reviewed and their mergeable/mergeStateStatus reconfirmed via `gh pr view` before a human merges either, rather than accepting this task's narrative at face value.
